objective: Proof and computation. The laws known to compose like cycles (KNOT-CIRCUITS Theorem 1: affine laws over fields, the coset laws of Z_{p^k}, S3 and D_p) are coset laws: every relation is a coset of a subgroup, so every fibre of every projection of every system has the same size; hence they are strongly balanced (Dyer-Richerby) and count in polynomial time, so none has mutual selection. Checked on Z3, Z4, GF(4) and S3: congruence criterion for cycle-like composition (Z2 x Z2 as control) and uniform fibres on random systems.
status: Proved by BEYOND-TWO-20261101-001A-P001: the laws known to compose like cycles (affine laws over fields; coset laws of Z_(p^k), S3, D_p) are coset laws, whose fibres all have one size, so they are strongly balanced and count in polynomial time (Dyer-Richerby): none has mutual selection; Theorem 1's criterion recomputed (Z3, Z4, GF(4), S3 yes; Z2 x Z2 no) and uniform fibres checked on 160 random coset systems
title: The known cycle-composing laws count easily
